title: Lesson 7: Installing and Deploying Hermes Agent: Local Setup, Profiles, Gateway, First Run
description: The consultant's deployment discipline: how to stand up an agent correctly once you have the go-ahead. Isolation per engagement, a verified first run before you layer on features, and a gateway that turns a laptop experiment into an always-on tool your client actually uses.

questions.question: Why deploy a separate profile for each engagement?
options: To make the agent respond faster on each machine
To share one set of credentials across every client
To reduce the number of installs you perform
To stop one client's state bleeding into another's
questions.explanation: A separate home per engagement keeps one client's prompts, memory, credentials, and state from contaminating another client's agent.

questions.question: What must happen before you add the gateway, cron, or skills?
options: Prove a clean conversation works before layering
Connect every platform the client might ever use
Turn on cron and skills so the system is complete
Install the desktop app alongside the command line
questions.explanation: Each feature you add is a variable, so the base conversation must be proven before any layer is trusted.

questions.question: What makes a deployment a real delivery rather than a prototype?
options: The agent works once during a demo on the consultant's laptop
The code and the data directory are stored on the same disk
The agent runs always-on in the client's own channel
The installer finished without reporting any errors
questions.explanation: A laptop terminal is a prototype; a delivery runs always-on and is reachable in the channel the client's team already uses.
